nodes.title: Tangents and Normals to Curves
points: Slope of tangent to curve y = f(x) at point P(x₁, y₁): m = (dy/dx)_(x₁, y₁).
Equation of Tangent: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).
Slope of Normal at P(x₁, y₁): m' = −1/m = −1 / (dy/dx)_(x₁, y₁) (provided m ≠ 0).
Equation of Normal: y − y₁ = (−1/m)(x − x₁).
Special Slopes: (1) Tangent parallel to X-axis ⟹ dy/dx = 0; (2) Tangent parallel to Y-axis (perpendicular to X-axis) ⟹ dx/dy = 0 (dy/dx = ∞).

nodes.title: Derivative as a Rate Measure
points: Displacement s = f(t) ⟹ Velocity v = ds/dt; Acceleration a = dv/dt = d²s/dt² = v (dv/ds).
Rate of change of quantity y with respect to x is dy/dx.
Spherical Balloon: Volume V = (4/3)π r³ ⟹ dV/dt = 4π r² (dr/dt); Surface Area S = 4π r² ⟹ dS/dt = 8π r (dr/dt).
Sliding Ladder (length L): x² + y² = L² ⟹ 2x(dx/dt) + 2y(dy/dt) = 0 ⟹ dy/dt = −(x/y)(dx/dt).
Water leaking from inverted cone (semi-vertical angle α): r = h tanα ⟹ V = (1/3)π r² h = (1/3)π tan²α h³.

nodes.title: Approximations Using Differentials
points: Formula: f(a + h) ≈ f(a) + h · f'(a), where h is a small change in x (h = Δx).
Steps to approximate f(x):
1. Identify function f(x) and choose 'a' close to given value such that f(a) and f'(a) are exact numbers.
2. Calculate h = x − a (h can be positive or negative).
3. Compute f'(x) and evaluate f'(a).
4. Substitute into f(a + h) ≈ f(a) + h f'(a).

nodes.title: Rolle's Theorem & Conditions
points: Statement: If a real-valued function f:[a, b] → ℝ satisfies:
1. f is CONTINUOUS on closed interval [a, b],
2. f is DIFFERENTIABLE on open interval (a, b),
Then there exists AT LEAST ONE point c ∈ (a, b) such that f'(c) = 0.
Geometric Interpretation: At point (c, f(c)), the tangent to the curve is HORIZONTAL (parallel to X-axis).

nodes.title: Lagrange's Mean Value Theorem (LMVT)
points: Statement: If a function f:[a, b] → ℝ satisfies:
1. f is CONTINUOUS on closed interval [a, b],
2. f is DIFFERENTIABLE on open interval (a, b),
Then there exists AT LEAST ONE point c ∈ (a, b) such that f'(c) = [f(b) − f(a)] / (b − a).
Geometric Interpretation: At point (c, f(c)), the tangent is PARALLEL to the secant line (chord) joining endpoints (a, f(a)) and (b, f(b)).
Rolle's theorem is a special case of LMVT where f(a) = f(b).

nodes.title: Increasing and Decreasing Functions
points: Let f be continuous on [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b):
Strictly Increasing on [a, b] ⟺ f'(x) > 0 for all x ∈ (a, b).
Strictly Decreasing on [a, b] ⟺ f'(x) < 0 for all x ∈ (a, b).
Monotonic Function: Either entirely non-increasing or non-decreasing.
Critical Points: Points where f'(x) = 0 or f'(x) does not exist.
Finding intervals: Set f'(x) = 0, find critical numbers, test sign of f'(x) on each sub-interval using sign chart.

nodes.title: Maxima and Minima (First & Second Derivative Tests)
points: First Derivative Test: Let c be critical point (f'(c) = 0):
(1) If f'(x) changes sign from + to − as x increases through c ⟹ Local MAXIMUM at c.
(2) If f'(x) changes sign from − to + as x increases through c ⟹ Local MINIMUM at c.
(3) If f'(x) does not change sign ⟹ Point of Inflection.
Second Derivative Test (Most commonly used):
(1) If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) < 0 ⟹ Local MAXIMUM at x = c; Maximum value = f(c).
(2) If f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) > 0 ⟹ Local MINIMUM at x = c; Minimum value = f(c).
(3) If f''(c) = 0, test is inconclusive (use First Derivative Test).

nodes.title: Applied Optimization Problems
points: Steps for Optimization Word Problems:
1. Draw diagram and define variables.
2. Write formula for quantity to be optimized (e.g., Area, Volume, Cost).
3. Use constraint equation to eliminate one variable, expressing quantity as function of single variable f(x).
4. Differentiate, set f'(x) = 0, find critical point.
5. Verify maximum/minimum using second derivative test f''(x).
6. Compute required dimensions and maximum/minimum value.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Questions
points: Board Favourite #1: Verify Rolle's Theorem for f(x) = x² − 4x + 3 on [1, 3] and find c.
Board Favourite #2: Verify LMVT for f(x) = x³ − 5x² − 3x on [1, 3] and find c.
Board Favourite #3: Find the approximate value of √(64.12) or tan⁻¹(1.002) using differentials.
Board Favourite #4: Word problem: An open box of maximum volume is made from a square sheet of side 24 cm by cutting equal squares from corners.
Board Favourite #5: Find equation of tangent and normal to curve x = a cos³θ, y = a sin³θ at θ = π/4.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Optimization Shortcuts & 10-Second Hacks
points: LMVT Midpoint Shortcut: For ANY quadratic function f(x) = Ax² + Bx + C on [a, b], value of c in LMVT is ALWAYS the EXACT MIDPOINT: c = (a + b) / 2.
Open Box Volume Hack: For a square sheet of side a, the cut-out corner square for maximum volume is ALWAYS x = a/6, and Max Volume = 2a³/27.
Largest Rectangle in Circle of radius R: It is ALWAYS a SQUARE of side R√2, with Maximum Area = 2R².
Largest Rectangle in Ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1: Maximum Area = 2ab, dimensions a√2 × b√2.
Wire Partition Trick: Wire of length L cut into two parts to form square and circle: For minimum combined area, side of square = 2 × radius of circle.
